title: Outcome-masked selection of a coarsened time grid for panel clone-censor-weight emulation
question: Within a prespecified two-year treatment-initiation setting, how much do causal estimates move when treatment, visit, covariate, and outcome histories are observed and modeled only on 1-, 2-, 4-, or 8-week grids; can an outcome-masked process rule choose a grid that reduces computation without materially worsening bias, coverage, precision, or treatment decisions relative to always choosing one week; and how much do estimates differ between separately defined 4- and 12-week grace-period strategies?
aims: This study settles only the time-grid selection and grid-movement part of TZO-01 within the simulated panel-data domain. It constructs separate coarsened data versions, fits resolution-specific nuisance models, quantifies systematic movement among expected estimates, and compares an outcome-blind selector with always choosing the finest grid under equal analysis-sample and equal total-resource budgets. It also reports the contrast between 4- and 12-week grace-period estimands. It does not select a clinically meaningful grace period, establish that either grace period is preferable, or claim that process data can identify a uniquely adequate grid for every outcome law.

dgm.covariates: Each replicate contains an independent outcome-masked design sample of 1000 people and an analysis sample of 4000 people. Everyone is eligible at week 0 and followed through week 104. Draw age from N(60, 10^2) truncated to 40 through 80 and define Xage=(age-60)/10. Draw female F from Bernoulli(0.50), comorbidity C from Bernoulli(0.35), latent state S0 from N(0.30 Xage+0.40 C-0.20 F,1), and recorded marker Z0=S0+N(0,0.15^2). At each weekly boundary k, untreated people initiate irreversible treatment with probability 1-exp[-exp(alphaA+0.75 Z+0.35 C+0.20 Xage-0.15 F+0.30 I(a visit occurred in the preceding week)+0.20 k/52)]. After that decision, latent state evolves as Sk=0.90 S(k-1)+0.05 Xage+0.08 C-0.04 F+N(0,0.35^2). Treatment does not affect the state. A visit occurs during week k with probability expit(alphaV+0.35 C+0.25 F+0.35 max(Z,0)+0.12 min(R,12)+0.10 sin(2 pi k/52)); its exact time is k+Uniform(0.05,0.95). At a visit, Z becomes Sk+N(0,0.15^2); otherwise Z is carried forward. The source history retains exact weekly treatment boundaries and visit times. Four separate analysis extracts are then created. A Delta-week extract contains only status and history available at boundaries of a 1-, 2-, 4-, or 8-week grid, with G and week 104 inserted as mandatory boundaries. It records treatment status at the boundary, whether any visit occurred in the preceding interval, the last marker available by the boundary, elapsed grid intervals since a visit, and whether the outcome occurred by the boundary. Exact within-bin treatment, visit, covariate, and outcome order is removed. Every grid-specific estimator and nuisance model receives only its corresponding extract. Exact source histories remain unavailable except to the explicitly labeled oracle benchmark and truth calculation.
dgm.outcome_model: The first nonfatal event follows a piecewise exponential model. During week k its rate per week is exp[-6.10+0.30 Xage+0.40 C-0.20 F+0.55 Sk+0.15 k/52+psi(s,C)], where s is time since initiation. An exponential waiting time supplies the exact event time. Follow-up ends at the first event or week 104. There is no competing event or loss to follow-up. Treatment and visit histories do not respond to the outcome. Grid extracts retain only the interval in which the event first became observable.
dgm.treatment_effect: Six prespecified profiles are used. The exact-null profile has psi(s,C)=0. The immediate-benefit stress profile has hazard ratios 0.60 for C=0 and 0.80 for C=1 from initiation onward. The biphasic stress profile has hazard ratios 1.40 and 1.60 during the first 2 weeks, 1.00 from weeks 2 through less than 6, and 0.55 and 0.75 thereafter. The delayed-smooth profile has no effect through week 4, a linear change on the log hazard scale from 1.00 to 0.60 or 0.80 between weeks 4 and 10, and the attained effect thereafter. The negligible-smooth profile changes linearly on the log hazard scale from 1.00 at initiation to 0.95 for C=0 or 0.98 for C=1 at week 8 and remains there. The off-grid profile has no effect through day 10, changes linearly to a hazard ratio of 1.20 or 1.30 by day 17, remains there through day 31, and changes linearly to 0.70 or 0.85 by day 45. These coefficients are fixed before simulation and are not solved to produce any selected grid, movement threshold, or decision reversal.
dgm.effect_modification: Comorbidity modifies each nonnull profile on the log hazard scale using the stratum-specific values stated in the treatment-effect specification. The null remains exactly null in both strata. For each visit-intensity and treatment-pressure combination, all six outcome profiles use identical baseline variables, latent states, visits, treatment starts, and selector inputs. Common exogenous random numbers couple the profiles wherever possible. The selector must therefore make the same choice for outcome-law twins that differ only in effect timing.

factors.name: Visit intensity
levels: Frequent: alphaV=-1.75, intended to produce approximately monthly observation
Sparse: alphaV=-3.45, intended to produce approximately one observation every 12 weeks
factors.rationale: The levels test whether a process-based selector responds to genuinely different observation densities. Realized visit distributions are reported, and no clinical representativeness is inferred from the nominal labels.

factors.name: Natural treatment pressure
factors.rationale: The levels create different adherence-weight and positivity burdens. Realized initiation probabilities, weight distributions, and effective sample sizes are reported instead of relying on nominal calibration.

factors.name: Outcome-effect timing
levels: Off-grid transient harm followed by benefit
factors.rationale: The profiles include null, negligible, delayed, smooth, abrupt, and differently aligned effects. Their treatment and visit laws are identical, and none is calibrated to force a material grid discrepancy. Immediate and biphasic effects are labeled stress tests rather than evidence about their prevalence in applications.

factors.name: Grace-period protocol
factors.rationale: These are illustrative short and long strategy windows. They define different interventions and estimands. The study assigns them no general clinical meaning and does not use their comparison to select G.

dgm.deliberately_true: The design is factorial over 2 visit intensities, 2 treatment pressures, 6 outcome profiles, and 2 grace protocols. Both grace protocols and all four analysis grids are evaluated on coupled source histories. Eligibility, assignment opportunities, and follow-up begin at week 0. Every extract preserves week 0, G, and week 104 as boundaries. Nuisance models are refitted from the information present at each resolution; no coarse-grid method receives hidden weekly histories. The number of person-period records and interval-specific nuisance parameters therefore increases as the grid becomes finer. Treatment and visit laws are identical across paired outcome profiles. The exact null contains no direct or mediated treatment effect. No coefficient is selected by examining simulated outcome performance.
dgm.cannot_detect: The study cannot choose a clinically meaningful grace period, establish a universally correct grid, or show how often grid dependence occurs in real emulations. It cannot identify outcome latency from treatment and visit processes alone. Its grid selector has domain-specific operating characteristics only. The design does not address competing risks, recurrent outcomes, fatal outcomes that alter care, multiple treatment versions, interference, unmeasured confounding, treatment-confounder feedback caused by treatment effects on health state, multiple visits within a week, subweekly treatment decisions, or source systems whose raw event times are already irreversibly rounded. Conclusions about clinical materiality require an externally elicited utility scale and are not supplied by this simulation.

estimands.name: Full-history two-year risk difference for grace period G
estimands.definition: For G equal to 4 or 12 weeks, gEarly,G permits natural initiation at weekly decisions before G and forces initiation at G among people still untreated. gDelay,G prevents initiation before G and returns to the natural initiation process at G. RDfull,G=P(TY at or before week 104 under gEarly,G)-P(TY at or before week 104 under gDelay,G). Negative values favor earlier initiation.
estimands.true_value_computation: For each structural mechanism, generate full weekly histories under both regimes with common exogenous random numbers. Conditional event risks are calculated from cumulative hazards rather than by repeatedly drawing event times. Truth generation proceeds in independent streaming batches of 250000 people until the paired Monte Carlo standard error is at most 0.00050. Failure to reach that precision within the prespecified compute allocation makes the affected cell uninformative.

estimands.name: Resolution-specific reported-data functional
estimands.definition: For each Delta in 1, 2, 4, and 8 weeks, RDpanel,G,Delta is the probability limit of the prespecified panel clone-censor-weight procedure when only the Delta-week extract is observed. The associated systematic approximation error is RDpanel,G,Delta-RDfull,G. This functional separates the result delivered by a particular coarsened protocol from the full-history causal target without pretending that all resolutions preserve identical information.
estimands.true_value_computation: Apply each frozen grid-specific procedure to an independent process and outcome population large enough to reduce the paired Monte Carlo standard error of every difference from RDfull,G below 0.00050. The calculation uses the same coarsening operator, nuisance-model specification, and boundary convention as the finite-sample estimator. An oracle-weight version is computed separately to distinguish temporal information loss from finite-sample nuisance estimation.

estimands.name: Change induced by changing the grace-period strategy
estimands.definition: DeltaG=RDfull,12-RDfull,4 on the absolute two-year risk scale. This is a contrast between two protocol-defined causal estimands, not movement of one fixed estimand under alternative analysis settings.
estimands.true_value_computation: Compute DeltaG from the coupled full-history intervention risks. Extend streaming truth batches until its paired Monte Carlo standard error is at most 0.00050. Grid-specific analogues are descriptive and are never used to choose G.

methods.name: Conventional prespecified four-week panel CCW
methods.point_estimator: Use only the four-week extract. At boundary tj, treatment and covariate status known at tj define adherence and the risk set for outcomes in (tj,tj+1]. A clone is censored before that next interval when a protocol deviation is observable at tj. A treatment start that first appears at tj+1 is never treated as if its hidden weekly time were known at tj. Fit a resolution-specific complementary-log-log initiation model containing interval indicators, baseline covariates, current recorded marker, prior-interval visit status, elapsed panel intervals since a visit, and the prespecified baseline interactions. Estimate arm risks with normalized weighted product-limit estimators and subtract them.
methods.variance_estimator: Stack the resolution-specific initiation-model score with both arm-specific weighted hazard scores. Use an original-person cluster sandwich to include clone dependence and estimated-weight uncertainty. Apply the delta method to the two risks and their difference.
methods.interval: Use an unbounded 95% Wald interval for RDpanel,G,4. Report treatment-first and outcome-first bounds for intervals in which treatment and outcome first become observable together. These bounds are sensitivity analyses and are not substituted for the primary panel convention.
methods.nonconvergence: Failure occurs if the grid-specific initiation model does not converge, produces a nonfinite coefficient, has a Hessian condition number above 1e12, produces a nonfinite weight, leaves an empty arm risk set, or produces a nonpositive or nonfinite sandwich variance. Extreme weights are reported separately.
methods.implementation: The method never receives exact weekly histories or exact within-bin event order. Primary weights are untruncated. Hard capping at 20 and empirical 1st- and 99th-percentile truncation are labeled sensitivity analyses.

methods.name: Prespecified coarsened-grid multiverse
methods.point_estimator: Repeat the panel CCW procedure independently on the 1-, 2-, 4-, and 8-week extracts. Each grid receives its own coarsened history and its own fitted nuisance model. Report the four estimates, all six paired differences, and Rmu=maxDelta E(RDhatDelta)-minDelta E(RDhatDelta). Estimate Rmu from the range of replicate-specific mean estimates, not from the mean of within-replicate ranges.
methods.variance_estimator: Within each grid, use the stacked original-person cluster sandwich. Across grids, retain paired replicate results and estimate the covariance of mean differences directly. Use a max-t Monte Carlo procedure for simultaneous confidence intervals covering all six paired expected-estimate differences.
methods.interval: Report 95% Wald intervals for individual grid functionals and simultaneous 95% Monte Carlo intervals for paired expected-estimate differences. Any within-dataset range is descriptive and is calibrated against its exact-null distribution.
methods.nonconvergence: Apply failure criteria separately by grid. Retain results from converged grids, report the pattern of failures, and require every grid to converge before calculating a cell's complete pairwise movement summary.
methods.implementation: Grid-specific data construction, nuisance fitting, scoring, and serialization are timed separately. Report person-period rows, nuisance-parameter count, peak memory, condition number, weight variability, effective sample size, and worker time. An oracle-weight analysis uses the same coarsened histories and known DGM transition probabilities to separate temporal information loss from nuisance-model error.

methods.name: Outcome-blind process-adaptive panel CCW
methods.point_estimator: Before any design-sample outcome is generated or revealed, construct its four process-only extracts. For each grid, estimate the proportion of nonempty bins containing more than one treatment or visit transition, the proportion containing both a marker update and treatment start, treatment-model calibration, predicted adherence-weight effective sample size, person-period count, and nuisance-parameter count. Select the coarsest grid whose one-sided 95% Wilson upper bounds for both aliasing proportions are at most 0.10, whose cross-validated process log loss per person-week is no more than 2% worse than the one-week grid, and whose predicted arm-specific effective sample size is at least 200. Select one week if no coarser grid passes. Freeze the rule, grid, thresholds, and fitted specification before revealing analysis outcomes. Apply the corresponding panel CCW estimator to the independent 4000-person analysis sample.
methods.variance_estimator: Use the locked grid's stacked original-person cluster sandwich. Because selection occurs in an independent outcome-masked sample, the interval is conditional on the selected grid. Empirical simulation evaluates the full two-sample procedure.
methods.interval: Use an unbounded 95% Wald interval for the selected grid's reported-data functional. Coverage for the full-history target is reported separately as approximation coverage and is not called nominal inferential coverage.
methods.nonconvergence: Failure occurs if process support is inadequate, no candidate has at least 50 treatment starts and 500 visits in the design sample, the locked nuisance or outcome model fails, a risk set is empty, or the sandwich variance is nonpositive or nonfinite. Falling back to one week after all coarser grids fail the quality criteria is a valid selection, not nonconvergence.
methods.implementation: The selector is run separately for each G because G is a mandatory boundary. Thresholds are fixed before outcome simulation and are not tuned using the 48 evaluation cells. The entire design-sample cost is included in runtime, memory, and total-data comparisons.

methods.name: Always-one-week comparators
methods.point_estimator: Apply the one-week panel CCW without selection to the same 4000-person analysis sample. Also apply it to the combined 5000 people after the selector has been locked, using the previously masked design-sample outcomes only for this resource-equivalent comparator. The first comparison isolates grid choice. The second gives always choosing one week the full participant budget consumed by the adaptive procedure.
methods.variance_estimator: Use the one-week stacked original-person cluster sandwich. Preserve paired results with the selected-grid estimator for bias, variance, mean squared error, and decision comparisons.
methods.interval: Use unbounded 95% Wald intervals for the one-week reported-data functional.
methods.nonconvergence: Use the same model, weight, risk-set, and sandwich criteria as the other panel estimators.
methods.implementation: Report the 4000-person and 5000-person results separately. Total-resource comparisons include process selection, fitting, scoring, and all participant records. The finest grid is therefore neither computationally free nor exempt from the data budget.

methods.name: Full-history exact-order oracle benchmark
methods.point_estimator: Use exact weekly treatment decisions, exact visit history, and exact event order. Censor a clone at the first known deviation before accepting any subsequent outcome. Apply forced treatment exactly at G. Estimate risks with exact-order weighted product-limit calculations using the correctly specified weekly initiation model.
methods.variance_estimator: Use the stacked original-person cluster sandwich with exact-time hazard increments and the weekly initiation-model score.
methods.interval: Use an unbounded 95% Wald interval for RDfull,G.
methods.nonconvergence: Use the same GLM, weight, risk-set, and sandwich criteria as the panel analyses.
methods.implementation: This is an oracle benchmark and is not presented as an available method when records are coarsened. It receives information withheld from every competing grid and is used only to quantify information loss and verify the one-week implementation.

performance.primary: For every scenario cell, estimate all six paired differences among the expected 1-, 2-, 4-, and 8-week estimates, their simultaneous 95% Monte Carlo intervals, the resulting range Rmu of expected estimates, and whether the outcome-blind selector is noninferior to the resource-equivalent always-one-week comparator while providing a measured computational advantage.
secondary: Bias and absolute bias relative to each resolution-specific reported-data functional
Approximation error relative to the full-history causal risk difference
Range of the four resolution-specific truths and range of the four expected estimates
Empirical standard error and mean model-based standard error
Relative error in the model-based standard error
Nominal coverage for the resolution-specific target
Approximation coverage for the full-history target, clearly labeled as nonnominal
Exact-null rejection rate and nonnull rejection rate
Bias, variance, and mean squared error relative to both always-one-week comparators
Treatment decisions and regret under the prespecified utility scale
Full-history and grid-specific DeltaG values with Monte Carlo uncertainty
Maximum weight, weight coefficient of variation, and arm-specific effective sample size
Person-period rows, nuisance-parameter count, peak memory, worker time, and serialization volume
Process-only aliasing proportions used by the selector
Within-dataset multiverse spread as a descriptive quantity after subtraction of its exact-null expectation
Treatment-first and outcome-first bounds for intervals with unresolved order
performance.n_rep_derivation: For coverage near 0.95, MCSE=sqrt[0.95(1-0.95)/R]. Requiring MCSE at most 0.005 gives R at least 1900, so 2000 replicates gives MCSE 0.00487. Coverage classifications use Monte Carlo confidence bounds rather than raw estimates. Paired replicate vectors are retained for max-t intervals on expected-estimate differences and for uncertainty in bias, mean squared error, runtime, and efficiency ratios.

decision_rule.problem_is_real_if: Decisions are cell-specific. Assign one loss unit to a two-year event and a fixed burden of 0.01 loss units to the earlier-treatment strategy. Early treatment is preferred when RDfull,G+0.01 is below zero. Set the grid-equivalence margin to 0.002 risk units, equal to 20% of the specified treatment burden. Grid choice is materially consequential in a cell if a simultaneous 95% Monte Carlo interval for any paired expected-estimate difference lies wholly above 0.002 or wholly below -0.002, or if simultaneous intervals place two grids on opposite sides of the utility decision boundary. A selector is a successful partial solution in that cell only if its absolute-bias deterioration relative to the 5000-person always-one-week comparator is no more than 0.002, the 95% Monte Carlo interval for its nominal coverage lies wholly within 0.925 to 0.975, the upper 95% Monte Carlo bound for its mean-squared-error ratio is at most 1.00, and the lower 95% bound for its reduction in total worker time is at least 25%. No count of affected cells is interpreted as prevalence in practice.
decision_rule.problem_is_not_real_if: Meaningful grid dependence is not demonstrated in a cell if every simultaneous 95% interval for paired expected-estimate differences lies wholly within -0.002 to 0.002 and every grid has the same utility-preferred action as the full-history truth. This is an equivalence conclusion for that cell only. It does not establish that a grace period can be selected or that grid choice is harmless outside the simulated domain.
decision_rule.uninformative_if: Classify a cell as uninformative if it lies between the separation and equivalence regions; if more than 5% of replicates fail for a required comparator; if median arm-specific effective sample size is below 100; if a truth Monte Carlo standard error exceeds 0.00050; if a coverage, bias, mean-squared-error, or runtime comparison crosses its decision boundary; or if the treatment decision under the full-history truth lies within 0.002 of the utility boundary. Report selector success or failure separately for every informative cell and make no catalog-wide prevalence claim.
decision_rule.both_branches_reachable: Under the exact-null profile, every population risk difference and every systematic grid difference can be zero, which permits the equivalence branch. Under nonnull profiles, honestly coarsened histories can produce expected differences larger than 0.002 or opposing utility decisions, which permits the material-consequence branch. Intermediate estimates, wide Monte Carlo intervals, and failures enter the uninformative branch. No branch requires one adverse scenario versus unanimity across all scenarios.

threats.threat: An outcome mechanism chosen to align with coarse boundaries could encode the desired finding.
threats.mitigation: Use six outcome laws that share identical treatment, visit, covariate, and selector inputs. Include null, negligible, delayed, smooth, abrupt, and off-grid effects. Freeze all coefficients without solving for grid movement or decision thresholds. Interpret the immediate and biphasic profiles only as stress tests.

threats.threat: Coarse extracts discard ordering that exists in the source history.
threats.mitigation: Discard the information consistently from every estimator fitted at that resolution. Define the panel boundary convention in advance, report treatment-first and outcome-first bounds for unresolved intervals, and label the exact-order method as an oracle rather than a fair data-available competitor.

threats.threat: Changing G changes the treatment strategy and causal estimand.
threats.mitigation: Define separate regimes and truths for each G. Report DeltaG only as a contrast between estimands. Never use outcome results or process intensity to select G.

threats.threat: Treatment and visit processes cannot reveal outcome latency or guarantee an adequate grid.
threats.mitigation: Force the selector to make identical choices for outcome-law twins with identical process histories. Interpret failures across the twins as evidence of the selector's domain limitation, not as a reason to retune it.

threats.threat: The selector consumes an additional design sample and could be dominated by always choosing one week.
threats.mitigation: Compare it with always one week on the same 4000-person analysis sample and on all 5000 available participants. Count selection costs in every resource measure. Require bias, coverage, mean-squared-error, and worker-time criteria before calling it a partial solution.

threats.threat: Fine grids may appear free if nuisance-model dimension and computational work are held constant.
threats.mitigation: Fit interval indicators and resolution-specific histories at every grid. Record model dimension, person-period rows, memory, runtime, convergence, weight dispersion, and effective sample size. Do not reuse the weekly nuisance fit in coarser analyses.

threats.threat: Nuisance-model misspecification could be mistaken for temporal-resolution bias.
threats.mitigation: Pair estimated-weight analyses with oracle-weight analyses using the same coarsened histories. Attribute discrepancies common to both to lost temporal information and discrepancies present only with estimated weights to nuisance estimation.

threats.threat: The four grids and 48 cells are not a probability sample from applied emulations.
threats.mitigation: Make decisions separately by cell. Any equal-weight summary is labeled a design average over the chosen factorial cells and is not interpreted as prevalence, frequency, or expected harm in practice.

threats.threat: The utility threshold is not an externally validated clinical threshold.
threats.mitigation: State the simulated utility scale explicitly and use it only for internal decision comparisons. Report risk-scale movements without calling them clinically important. Application-specific use requires external elicitation of event and treatment burdens.

threats.threat: Artificial-censoring weights may become unstable when initiation is uncommon.
threats.mitigation: Factor treatment pressure explicitly; report untruncated primary results, convergence, maximum weights, and effective sample sizes; and repeat analyses with a hard cap of 20 and empirical 1st- and 99th-percentile truncation.

threats.threat: The one-week source process omits subweekly treatment decisions and more complex observation patterns.
threats.mitigation: Limit conclusions to weekly treatment opportunities with at most one visit per week. List subweekly decisions, multiple same-week visits, and irreversibly rounded source records as untested settings.

threats.threat: The computational burden may exceed available resources.
threats.mitigation: Treat runtime as unknown until compiled-kernel benchmarks are complete. Benchmark generation, each grid-specific fit, stacked scoring, sensitivities, truth calculation, memory, and serialization separately. Freeze an outcome-independent feasibility decision before the main results are examined.

threats.threat: Software mistakes could create apparent grid differences.
threats.mitigation: Unit-test hand-constructed histories at every resolution; verify that no coarse estimator receives hidden source fields; check exact-null truths; require agreement of independent truth batches; save seeds and failure records; and compare the one-week implementation with the exact-history benchmark in trajectories without within-week ordering conflicts.

runtime_estimate: Runtime is unknown until benchmarking and is not represented by an unsupported point estimate. Before the main run, execute 100 timing-only replicates covering both visit intensities, both treatment pressures, all four grids, both grace periods, the selector, oracle weights, score construction, sensitivities, and serialization. Separately time 250000-person truth batches. Extrapolate worker-hours and peak memory by component, report medians and 95th percentiles, include a 25% rerun reserve, and freeze the compute allocation before examining performance results. If the upper projected worker-hour or memory requirement exceeds the reserved resources, classify the protocol as infeasible and revise it before starting the 2000-replicate evaluation. Replicate count and truth-precision requirements may not be reduced after outcome performance is inspected.

bears_on.what: The study evaluates the time-grid selection and grid-movement subproblem using genuinely resolution-specific data, nuisance models, statistical costs, and resource comparators. It reports changes between distinct grace-period estimands but does not select a clinically meaningful grace period or claim to resolve that component.

resolved.finding: The original grids changed only delayed censoring while retaining exact weekly histories and a common nuisance model.
resolved.what_changed: Each grid now receives a separately coarsened treatment, visit, covariate, and outcome extract. Nuisance models are refitted at that resolution, and model dimension, person-period volume, weight behavior, memory, and runtime vary with grid fineness.

resolved.finding: The study cannot select a clinically meaningful grace period and therefore cannot settle all of TZO-01.
resolved.what_changed: The title, question, aims, bears_on relation, decision rule, and limitations now state that the study settles only the time-grid selection and movement subproblem. The two grace periods remain distinct illustrative estimands, and no procedure or preference for selecting G is claimed.

resolved.finding: Instantaneous treatment effects combined with deliberately delayed censoring encoded the nonnull discrepancy.
resolved.what_changed: Known deviations are no longer deliberately censored late. All grid methods use only honestly coarsened information. Null, negligible, delayed, smooth, abrupt, and off-grid effect profiles are paired on identical process histories, fixed without calibrating coefficients to movement thresholds, and abrupt profiles are labeled stress tests.

resolved.finding: The status quo comparator was a deliberately degraded hybrid that knew the exact treatment time but ignored it.
resolved.what_changed: The fixed-grid comparator no longer receives exact treatment or event order. It applies a prespecified panel-boundary convention to information genuinely available at the selected resolution. Exact histories are confined to an explicitly labeled oracle benchmark.

resolved.finding: The selector was not compared with always choosing one week or charged for its additional design sample.
resolved.what_changed: Always-one-week comparators now use both the same 4000-person analysis sample and the full 5000-person resource budget. Selector success requires noninferior bias, coverage, and mean squared error plus a measured worker-time advantage after including selection costs.

resolved.finding: Mean within-replicate multiverse range was noise-inflated and could establish a problem when grid estimators had identical expectations.
resolved.what_changed: The decisive measure is now the range of expected grid estimates, estimated from paired replicate means with simultaneous max-t intervals. Within-dataset spread is descriptive and centered against its exact-null expectation.

resolved.finding: Arbitrary thresholds and counts of selected factorial cells were used as prevalence-like evidence.
resolved.what_changed: The protocol defines an explicit simulated utility scale and a grid-equivalence margin tied to that scale. Decisions are made separately for each cell. Counts and equal-weight summaries cannot support claims about prevalence in applications.

resolved.finding: The ordering-conflict diagnostic used an underpowered set of scenario cells and mechanically reused the outcomes producing the discrepancy.
resolved.what_changed: Outcome-based sensitivity and specificity claims and the O4 classifier were removed. The selector uses only process aliasing, process-model loss, support, and resource measures. Grid movement is measured directly after outcomes are unlocked.

resolved.finding: Coverage near 0.93 or 0.97 was classified from raw estimates despite substantial Monte Carlo uncertainty.
resolved.what_changed: Coverage decisions now require the 95% Monte Carlo interval to lie wholly within the prespecified acceptance region.

resolved.finding: The original wall-time estimate was unsupported and likely optimistic.
resolved.what_changed: Runtime is declared unknown pending component-level benchmarks. A timing-only pilot, uncertainty-bearing extrapolation, resource reserve, and outcome-independent feasibility gate are required before the main run.

resolved.finding: The Epidemiology citation incorrectly named Sperling as first author.
resolved.what_changed: The first author is corrected to Sperrin, and the title, journal, year, and DOI are supplied.

resolved.finding: Evidence from 14 DPP-4 inhibitor studies was generalized to clinical plausibility across an unspecified domain.
resolved.what_changed: The incomplete review citation and its generalized clinical claim were removed. Four and 12 weeks are now explicitly illustrative strategy windows with no asserted clinical representativeness.

resolved.finding: The PDS and Wanis references were bibliographically incomplete.
resolved.what_changed: Neither incomplete citation is used. The protocol retains only references whose bibliographic identity and stable identifier are supplied by the payload.

declared_limitations: The study does not select or validate a clinically meaningful grace period.
The study answers only the time-grid selection and grid-movement part of TZO-01 within the prespecified panel-data domain.
Treatment and observation processes alone cannot guarantee that a selected grid preserves outcome-relevant timing under every outcome law.
The factorial cells are not a probability sample of applied emulations, so their counts do not estimate prevalence or expected harm in practice.
The simulated utility scale is an internal decision device and does not establish clinical materiality.

The results do not cover subweekly treatment decisions, multiple same-week visits, competing or recurrent outcomes, fatal events that change care, treatment-confounder feedback, interference, unmeasured confounding, or irreversibly rounded source records.
Runtime and feasibility remain unestablished until the prespecified compiled-kernel and full-replicate benchmarks pass.
